key_insight: Using multiple ParameterNets in neural implicit flow improves reacting-flow super-resolution accuracy over a single ParameterNet without increasing the reported hyperparameter cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports reconstruction of fine-resolution species and temperature fields from coarse combustion data.
method: Reconfigure neural implicit flow inputs and outputs for multiscalar super-resolution.
Use nonlinear principal component analysis to represent composition in a latent space and reconstruct species and temperature fields.
Assign a separate ParameterNet to each nonlinear principal component.
evidence_signal: Validation on a 2D unsteady, inlet-forced, lean premixed methane–air Bunsen flame used a coarsening ratio of 8 in a given direction and favored multiple ParameterNets.
watch_item: Generalization to 3D flames, other fuels, and different combustion regimes is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: A Neural Implicit Flow Super-Resolution Approach for Reacting Flows
